title: Growth playbook: manager asks, experiments, and evidence log
content:
Notes-to-self: quick orientation

Purpose: quick, portable playbook to use in manager syncs. Bring explicit asks that are measurable and experiment-focused. This is intentionally short and modular so I can copy sections into Slack/PRD drafts.

Current posture (one-liner): leading cross-functional ops projects, shipping two process automations, coaching 2 PMs; want to grow into strategic program lead and manager-of-managers basics over next 12 months.

Early signals I care about (what I will point to in a calibration convo):
- Programs launched with cross-org adoption >= 3 teams in first 90 days.
- Two reproducible onboarding docs/templates I authored adopted by Solutions Eng and CS.
- Evidence of up-leveling: at least 1 direct report promoted or expanded role responsibility in 6-9 months.
- Time spend: reduce repetitive execution by 10–15% (freeing time for strategy).

Hypotheses I want to test (experiment orientation):
1) Structured delegation hypothesis: creating a 15-min weekly 'handoff card' per project will accelerate direct report autonomy and reduce my tactical tasking.
   - Experiment: run for 8 weeks across 3 projects.
   - Signal: number of decisions made without my intervention increases by 30% (tracked via project decision log).
2) Office hours for cross-org unblock hypothesis: 1x90m drop-in reduces escalation tickets by 25% in the teams I support.
   - Metric: tickets labeled "ops-escalation" resolved without manager intervention.
3) Narrative-building hypothesis: weekly one-pager for the exec team improves visibility and leads to 1 strategic ask being approved in Q2.

Concrete manager asks (ready to paste into a sync):
- Time & sponsorship: 1-2 hours / week of your time for 6 weeks to co-sponsor the cross-team delegation pilot. Outcome: experimental report and recommended operating model.
- Promotion calibration: block 30 min in calibration cycle to discuss promotion case for Lina (direct) — I will bring a written case and evidence artifacts.
- Exposure: an intro email connecting me with VP Product for a 20-min exploratory chat about product-ops partnership by end of month.
- Headcount ask framing: allow me to trial a 6-week contractor to offload execution tasks for project X so I can run a strategic pilot.

Evidence I will bring / artifacts (short list):
- project decision log (spreadsheet rows with timestamp, decision, owner)
- two onboarding templates (links to Google docs)
- pilot retrospective (one-pager)
- 1:1 coaching notes with development outcomes (anonymized)

30 / 60 / 90 plan (what success looks like for next 3 months):
- 30d: finalize delegation templates, run orientation with two directs, baseline measurement. Deliverable: delegation template + decision log initial entries.
- 60d: pilot in flight for 3 projects, run office hours, collect mid-pilot data. Deliverable: interim memo with metrics and examples.
- 90d: synthesize learnings, propose operating model & ask for headcount/scale. Deliverable: executive one-pager + ask language for you to escalate.

Signals-to-watch (red / amber / green):
- Green: directs make independent decisions >50% of time on routine tasks; cross-org adoption of template >2 teams.
- Amber: partial autonomy but recurring clarifying questions; pilot adoption limited.
- Red: I remain primary decision owner; no reduction in my tactical time.

Risks and mitigation (short):
- Risk: pilot perceived as offloading rather than upskilling. Mitigation: explicit training sessions + co-owned decision rubric.
- Risk: requests look like headcount avoidance. Mitigation: frame contractor as temporary capacity to gather evidence for headcount.

Manager talking points (script snippets):
- "I'd like your sponsorship for a tight experiment to increase delegation. It will run for 8 weeks and I can show you baseline vs end-state metrics before you commit to scaling."
- "If you can introduce me to VP Product, I want to explore a small cross-team scope that could be a low-cost win for Q2."

Quick checklist before manager sync (10 min prep):
- [ ] Attach delegation template + one example decision log row
- [ ] Draft 30/60/90 and highlight the 60d milestone as a review point
- [ ] Prepare one short anecdote that shows current bottleneck (30s)
- [ ] List explicit asks (time, intro, contractor approval, promotion calendar slot)

Notes-to-self: phrasing to avoid
- Avoid vague career language like "more strategic work" without concrete outcomes.
- Don't ask for "support" — ask for "sponsorship" or "time to review".

Open questions / things to research before next sync:
- What is typical response time from manager on headcount contractor pilots? (check previous hires / finance policy)
- Are there existing delegation templates in People Ops shared drive? (Confluence search)

Mini log (experiments & dates):
- 2026-01-25: Launched decision log template (seeded 3 rows). Early notes: team confused about what merits escalation.
- 2026-02-08: Office hours pilot started (first two drop-ins). Results: resolved 4 quick escalations, 1 follow-up needed.
- 2026-02-22: Drafted one-pager for exec; requested feedback from Aisha.

Personal reflection: what will change if this works?
- I'll shift from "doer" to "designer" for ops programs; more time for partnership conversations that influence roadmaps.

Tiny next actions (today):
- Copy delegation template into shared doc + annotate examples (30m).
- Send calendar invite to manager for a 20-min sync (ask: 1 specific intro + 30-min calibration time).

End-of-doc note: keep this file short, update log entries weekly, and when the experiment completes create a final public retrospective in team drive.
